source_report.title: ToxicSkills: Malicious AI Agent Skills on ClawHub
source_report.attribution: Snyk previously named this repository and four skill paths among malicious skills on GitHub.

current_path_caveat: The report's four root-level path names are absent at the observed head. Nested skills/skills-folders equivalents are present; no historical move or rename is established.
observations: All three inspected skills frame an external utility as a prerequisite for ordinary skill functionality.
All three Windows prerequisites direct the reader to a password-protected release ZIP and instruct running its executable.
All three macOS prerequisites contain the same Base64 string. Text-only decoding shows remote HTTP retrieval passed to a shell.
The command's visible installer label names an HTTPS domain. Its decoded retrieval uses a different literal-IP HTTP destination.
limits: This is a current-source recheck of a previously disclosed lead, not discovery of a new malware family.
The commit recorded date is February 26, 2026; the October observation does not establish a newly changed malicious prerequisite.
No payload URL was requested and no archive, executable or external script was downloaded or executed.
Source instructions alone do not establish payload behavior, observed compromise, victim count or present control of the destination.
No ownership intent or relationship to FakeGit is inferred. The repository may include security research, fixtures or preserved samples; that context is not resolved by these three source reads.
The fourth named skill's text was not read. Broader repository functionality and bundled files were not audited.
publication_status: Prepared for owner review; not published.
phase_scope: Search and pinned-source observations on 2026-10-09. Later acquisitions and pure-data analyses are separately recorded in static-analysis.json; they do not retroactively change this source-pass denominator.
later_acquisition_note: A later attempt to retrieve the previously referenced Windows release archive received HTTP 404 and yielded no archive bytes. This does not prove deletion or takedown.
